mainTopic: רב הונא on a גט with a spoken condition according to רבי יוסי, and his rule that a sick man's גט, like his gift, is cancelled if he recovers.
overview: The amud opens with רב הונא's doubt about a husband who adds a spoken condition to his גט. At first the גמרא says he was unsure whether רבי יוסי's rule, that the date on a document proves when it takes effect, applies in that case. A ברייתא about 'our Rabbis' shows that רבי יוסי does apply it. So the doubt is restated: does the הלכה follow רבי יוסי here? A ruling of רבא seems to settle this. The גמרא answers either that רבא was sure while רב הונא was not, or that רבא follows the רבנן and is only teaching how certain phrases are read. A second version puts רב הונא's statement on the 'after my death' case: according to רבי יוסי she must do חליצה, because רבי יוסי and רבי each hold their own view. Then the גמרא turns to a new line of the משנה, about a sick man's גט. רב הונא teaches that a sick man's גט works like his deathbed gift, so a real recovery cancels it. When the משנה seems to contradict this, the גמרא explains that the משנה's man never truly recovered and only walked leaning on his cane.

steps.title: Stating רב הונא's doubt about רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא was unsure whether רבי יוסי's rule about the date of a document applies even when the husband adds a spoken condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא was unsure whether רבי יוסי said his rule even about a spoken condition, or whether he did not say it in that case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly what רב הונא was unsure about. The question is whether רבי יוסי's rule about the date on a document still works when the husband attaches a condition out loud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי holds that the date written on a document shows when it takes effect. רב הונא wonders whether that is still true when the husband adds a spoken condition that is not written in the גט. If it is not true, the גט might only take effect later, when the condition is fulfilled.

keyTerms.meaning: Spoken out loud, not written in the document
Whether ... or not; the wording of a doubt

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּעַל פֶּה,
phrases.english: whether Rabbi Yosei says [his rule] about a spoken [condition],
phrases.notes: This continues the previous lines. The person who is unsure is רב הונא, and 'his rule' means 'the date on a document proves when it takes effect.'

phrases.english: or whether he does not say it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּעַל פֶּה, אִי לָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the explanation of רב הונא's doubt from the lines before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא's doubt is whether רבי יוסי applies זמנו של שטר מוכיח עליו when there is a spoken condition.

steps.title: Challenge from the case of 'if I have not come back in twelve months'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב הונא could be unsure. It cites a משנה about a spoken condition and a ברייתא in which 'our Rabbis' permitted the woman to remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is he really unsure? We learned in a משנה: 'This is your גט if I have not come back within twelve months,' and he died within the twelve months. It is not a גט. And a ברייתא taught about this: our Rabbis permitted her to marry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that רב הונא's doubt is about what רבי יוסי holds. It starts bringing a source in which a spoken condition was made and 'our Rabbis' still let the woman remarry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the condition 'if I have not come back' is spoken, not written in the גט. The משנה says it is not a גט, so she would still be tied to יבום. 'Our Rabbis' disagree and let her remarry, which means they treat the גט as taking effect from its written date, before he died. The next step will show who 'our Rabbis' are.

keyTerms.meaning: Is he really unsure? A challenge that he should already know the answer
And a ברייתא taught about it
'Our Rabbis', a group of Sages quoted in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two opinions. The משנה says the גט does not work. 'Our Rabbis' in the ברייתא say it does work, so she may remarry. The challenge is built on 'our Rabbis.'

phrases.english: But is he uncertain?!
But didn't we learn in a משנה:
"This is hereby your bill of divorce
if I have not come back
from now until twelve months [are over],"
and he died within the twelve months,
it is not a [valid] bill of divorce.
And a ברייתא taught about it:
Our Rabbis permitted her to marry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the description of רב הונא's doubt given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב הונא is unsure whether רבי יוסי applies his rule to a spoken condition.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a known case with a spoken condition in which Sages who follow רבי יוסי treated the גט as valid from its date. So רבי יוסי's view is already clear.

steps.title: 'Our Rabbis' follow רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls that 'our Rabbis' are the court that permitted gentile oil, and that they follow רבי יוסי's rule about the date of a document.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we said: who are 'our Rabbis'? רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the court that permitted oil, and they hold like רבי יוסי, who said the date of a document proves when it takes effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge. It shows that 'our Rabbis', who permitted her to remarry, base their ruling on רבי יוסי's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Those Sages let the woman remarry even though the condition was spoken. They did this because they follow רבי יוסי's rule that the date on a document proves when it takes effect. So רבי יוסי clearly applies his rule even with a spoken condition, and רב הונא should have nothing to be unsure about.

keyTerms.meaning: And we said, recalling an earlier discussion
The court that permitted oil made by non-Jews
The date of a document proves when it takes effect

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the step that turns the ברייתא into real proof. It links the ruling of 'our Rabbis' directly to רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: And we said: who are 'our Rabbis'?
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
the court that permitted oil;
phrases.notes: This is the court that permitted using oil made by non-Jews.

phrases.english: and they hold like Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: זְמַנּוֹ שֶׁל שְׁטָר מוֹכִיחַ עָלָיו.
phrases.english: who said: the date of a document proves [when it takes effect].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof inside the קשיא of step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי applies his rule even when the condition is spoken.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's identification of 'our Rabbis' as followers of רבי יוסי, who permitted remarriage in the case of the משנה, which has a spoken condition.

steps.title: רב הונא's doubt is about the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא restates רב הונא's doubt. He knows what רבי יוסי holds, but he is unsure whether the הלכה follows רבי יוסי when there is a spoken condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he is unsure whether the הלכה follows רבי יוסי when the condition is spoken, or whether the הלכה does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing what the doubt was about. The doubt is no longer about רבי יוסי's opinion. It is about whether we rule like him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא proved what רבי יוסי holds, so that cannot be the doubt. רב הונא's question now is practical. Do we follow רבי יוסי in a case with a spoken condition, or not?

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה does not follow him

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא is not unsure about what רבי יוסי holds. He is unsure whether the הלכה follows רבי יוסי when the husband adds a spoken condition.

phrases.english: Rather, he is uncertain

phrases.aramaic: אִי הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּעַל פֶּה,
phrases.english: whether the הלכה follows Rabbi Yosei with a spoken [condition],
or the הלכה does not [follow him].

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ אִי הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 2 and 3 by changing what the doubt is about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the doubt, from what רבי יוסי holds to whether the הלכה follows him.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא was unsure what רבי יוסי himself holds about a spoken condition.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי's view is clear. רב הונא is unsure whether the הלכה follows it in a case with a spoken condition.

steps.title: How can רב הונא be unsure? רבא already ruled on this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא's doubt using a ruling of רבא about which wordings make a valid conditional גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is he really unsure? But רבא said: 'This is your גט if I die' or 'when I am dead' is a valid גט. 'When I die' or 'after death' is not a valid גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא's doubt by quoting a ruling of רבא. רבא seems to have already decided this question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says that some wordings ('if I die,' 'when I am dead') make the גט valid, and other wordings ('when I die,' 'after death') make it invalid. At this point the גמרא only quotes the ruling. The next steps will show why it seems to settle רב הונא's doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Is he really unsure? (a challenge, not a real question)

steps.confusionAlert: 'When I am dead' (valid) and 'when I die' (not valid) sound almost the same in English. רבא treats them differently, and step 9 comes back to these two phrases.

phrases.english: But is he really unsure?!
phrases.notes: 'He' is רב הונא, from the earlier steps.

phrases.english: But didn't Rava say:
"This is your bill of divorce if I die"
or "when I am dead" – this is a valid bill of divorce.
"When I die" or "after death" – this is not a bill of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the doubt that was restated in Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's doubt about whether the הלכה follows רבי יוסי when there is a spoken condition.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא's ruling seems to already decide the question, so how can רב הונא still be unsure?

steps.title: What case is רבא talking about? Not one where he said 'from today'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case רבא means. It rejects the idea that the husband said 'from today,' because then רבא would only be repeating a משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say the husband told her 'from today,' following the רבנן, does that need to be said? We already learned in the משנה: 'From today, if I die' is a valid גט!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא works out what case רבא must be talking about. Here it rules out the first possibility, and this sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband said 'from today,' even the רבנן agree the גט is valid, and the משנה already says so. רבא would be adding nothing new, so his ruling cannot be about that case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
Does it need to be said? (meaning it is obvious)

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say that he told her "from today,"
and it follows the Rabbis, does that need to be said?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתְנַן: ״מֵהַיּוֹם אִם מַתִּי״ – הֲרֵי זֶה גֵּט!
phrases.english: But we learned: "From today, if I die" – it is a valid bill of divorce!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out the case behind רבא's ruling so the challenge in Step 5 can be completed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what case did רבא give his ruling?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not a case where the husband said 'from today,' because the משנה already covers that case.

steps.title: So רבא must hold the הלכה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבא must mean a case where the husband did not say 'from today.' That case only works according to רבי יוסי, so the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it a case where he did not say 'from today,' and it follows רבי יוסי? Learn from this that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge. רבא's ruling must follow רבי יוסי, so the question רב הונא was unsure about is already decided.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the words 'from today,' only רבי יוסי's rule about the date of the document makes the גט take effect from now. Since רבא rules the גט is valid even with a spoken condition, the הלכה follows רבי יוסי. That is exactly what רב הונא was unsure about.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it a case where he did not tell her "from today,"
and it follows Rabbi Yosei?
Learn from this: the halacha follows Rabbi Yosei!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא לָאו דְּלָא אָמַר לַהּ מֵהַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge, now that the 'from today' case has been ruled out.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה follows רבי יוסי even when there is a spoken condition.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's ruling, which can only be explained as following רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Clear to רבא, uncertain to רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: First answer: רבא was sure about this, and רב הונא was not. They simply disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: To רבא it is obvious. To רב הונא it is uncertain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by accepting it. רבא really does hold like רבי יוסי, but רב הונא never claimed to be following רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing forces רב הונא to share רבא's certainty. Two אמוראים can see the same question differently. One is sure, and the other stays in doubt.

phrases.english: To Rava it is obvious,
to Rav Huna it is uncertain.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרָבָא פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ לְרַב הוּנָא מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 5 to 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The two אמוראים disagree: one is sure, the other is in doubt.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's ruling should settle רב הונא's doubt.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא is sure the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, but רב הונא can still be unsure.

steps.title: Or: רבא follows the רבנן and is teaching how to read the wording
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: רבא is talking about a case where the husband did say 'from today,' following the רבנן. His new point is how certain phrases should be read.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: really, he told her 'from today,' and it follows the רבנן. רבא needed to teach about these phrases: 'when I am dead' is like 'if I die,' and 'when I die' is like 'after death.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer. רבא's ruling has nothing to do with רבי יוסי at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in Step 6 was 'this is already in the משנה.' The answer is that the משנה does not mention the phrases 'when I am dead' and 'when I die.' רבא teaches that the first is treated like 'if I die' (valid), and the second like 'after death' (not valid). So רבא adds something new, and nothing can be proven about רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces a second answer)
Really, actually (keeps the option that was rejected earlier)

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers: (1) רבא is sure the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, while רב הונא is unsure. (2) רבא follows the רבנן with 'from today,' and is only teaching that 'when I am dead' = 'if I die' (valid) and 'when I die' = 'after death' (not valid).
steps.whyThisMatters: The second answer means רבא's ruling can't prove anything about רבי יוסי. So whether the הלכה follows him with a spoken condition may still be an open question.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
Really, he told her "from today," and it follows the Rabbis,
and he needed to teach these expressions:
"When I am dead" is like "if I die";
"When I die" is like "after death."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא לְעוֹלָם דַּאֲמַר לַהּ מֵהַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate answer to the same challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives רבא's ruling a different case and a different new point.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Reading רבא as following the רבנן would make his ruling repeat the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא follows the רבנן and teaches how new phrases are read, so no proof for רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Another version: רב הונא on the 'after my death' case
steps.stepSummary: Some teach רב הונא's statement on a different clause of the משנה. If the husband said 'This is your גט after my death,' he said nothing. Still, according to רבי יוסי, she must do חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some people teach רב הונא's statement on the later clause of the משנה: 'This is your גט after my death' means he said nothing. רב הונא said: But according to רבי יוסי, she must do חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of where רב הונא's statement belongs. Here, רב הונא says that according to רבי יוסי, the 'after my death' case still needs חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי holds that the date written on a גט counts as if the husband said 'from today.' So for him, 'after my death' works like 'from today and after my death,' and that case is in doubt. Because the גט might be valid, she cannot do יבום, so she must do חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: And some teach it (this statement) on a different place
The later clause of a משנה
He said nothing; his words have no legal effect
She does חליצה, the release from יבום

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the same statement of רב הונא, placed on a different line of the משנה. So it now means something a little different.

phrases.english: And there are those who teach it on the later clause:
phrases.notes: 'It' means רב הונא's statement from before.

phrases.english: 'This is your bill of divorce after death'
– he said nothing.
Rav Huna said:
But according to Rabbi Yosei, she performs ḥalitza.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רב הונא's statement. In this version there is no doubt to challenge with רבא's ruling, so the earlier back-and-forth does not apply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, a גט given 'after my death' still requires חליצה.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that רב הונא's statement is obvious. The רבנן require חליצה when he said 'from today and after death.' So רבי יוסי, who treats a plain 'after death' like 'from today,' must also require חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is obvious! From the later clause, we know that according to the רבנן she does חליצה. So in the earlier clause too, according to רבי יוסי she does חליצה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב הונא needed to say this at all, since it seems to follow automatically.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only thing רבי יוסי and the רבנן argue about is whether the husband must actually say 'from today.' For the רבנן, 'from today and after death' leads to חליצה. For רבי יוסי, 'after death' already counts as 'from today and after death.' So he should also require חליצה, and רב הונא seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; why say it?

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'later clause' means the case where he said 'from today and after death.' 'Earlier clause' means the plain 'after death' case that רב הונא spoke about.

phrases.english: It is obvious,
since from the later clause – according to the Rabbis she performs ḥalitza,
in the earlier clause as well – according to Rabbi Yosei she performs ḥalitza!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רב הונא's statement in the second version teaches anything new.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רב הונא's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's view follows directly from the רבנן's ruling, so stating it is unnecessary.

steps.title: We might have thought רבי יוסי agrees with רבי
steps.stepSummary: The statement is needed. Otherwise we might think רבי יוסי agrees with רבי, who says such a גט is fully valid with no חליצה. רב הונא teaches that the two do not share a view.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that here רבי יוסי holds like רבי, who says it is a fully valid גט and no חליצה is needed. So רב הונא teaches us that רבי does not hold like רבי יוסי, and רבי יוסי does not hold like רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what new point רב הונא is teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that 'from today and after death' is a complete גט. Since רבי יוסי is also lenient about the 'from today' wording, we might group him with רבי and say no חליצה is needed. רב הונא teaches that רבי יוסי stays with the doubt, so חליצה is required.

phrases.english: Lest you say,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּהָא כְּרַבִּי סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
phrases.english: that in this, Rabbi Yosei holds like Rabbi,
– who says: it is a proper bill of divorce,
and ḥalitza is also not needed;
he teaches us

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא רַבִּי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: that Rabbi does not hold like Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yosei does not hold like Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'it is obvious' challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a mistaken idea that the statement prevents
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי agrees with רבי that the גט is fully valid, so no חליצה is needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי holds his own view, which leaves the גט in doubt, so חליצה is required.

steps.title: Each one's 'like this' excludes the other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the point. רבי says 'a case like this is a גט' to exclude רבי יוסי's view. רבי יוסי says 'a case like this is a גט' to exclude רבי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי does not hold like רבי יוסי, because it teaches: 'Like this, it is a גט,' to exclude רבי יוסי. And רבי יוסי does not hold like רבי, because it teaches: 'Like this, it is a גט,' to exclude רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows from the wording of each Sage's own statement that he is deliberately setting himself apart from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'like this' (כָּזֶה) means 'only in a case like this.' Each רב uses it to limit his ruling to his own case. That shows each one rejects the other's ruling. So the two views really are separate, as רב הונא taught.

keyTerms.meaning: Like this; only a case like this one

steps.whatToRemember: רבי and רבי יוסי each hold a separate view, and each uses the word 'like this' (כָּזֶה) to rule out the other. So according to רבי יוסי, a גט 'after my death' is in doubt and she must do חליצה.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי לָא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
phrases.english: Rabbi does not hold like Rabbi Yosei
– as it teaches: 'Like this – it is a bill of divorce,'
to exclude that of Rabbi Yosei;

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי לָא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yosei does not hold like Rabbi
– as it teaches: 'Like this – it is a bill of divorce,'
to exclude that of Rabbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי לָא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives proof for the answer in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי and רבי יוסי hold separate views
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'like this' (כָּזֶה) in each of their statements, which limits each ruling and excludes the other's view.

steps.title: The source for רבי's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows where רבי's view comes from: a ברייתא where he says 'from today and after death' is a full גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי's view? A ברייתא teaches: if the husband says 'from today and after death,' the חכמים say it is a doubtful גט. רבי says a case like this is a full גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just said that רבי and רבי יוסי each said 'a case like this is a גט.' Now it shows the exact ברייתא where רבי said it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים are unsure whether 'from today' or 'after death' counts, so the גט is only a doubt and she must do חליצה. רבי says the words 'from today' make it a full גט, so no חליצה is needed. This is the view that רב הונא said רבי יוסי does not share.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? Where is this view found?
A גט and not a גט — a doubtful divorce
A case like this is a valid גט

phrases.english: What is the view of רבי?
As it is taught in a ברייתא:
"From today and after death" —
it is a גט and it is not a גט, these are the words of the חכמים;
רבי says: a case like this is a גט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the source for רבי's phrase 'a case like this is a גט' mentioned in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי's 'a case like this is a גט' refers to 'from today and after death.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי argues with the חכמים.

steps.title: The source for רבי יוסי's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows where רבי יוסי's view comes from: a משנה about a גט written within twelve months and given after.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי יוסי's view? A משנה teaches: a man said, 'Write and give a גט to my wife if I do not come back within twelve months.' They wrote it within the twelve months and gave it after. The חכמים say it is not a גט. רבי יוסי says a case like this is a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא shows the other case, the one where רבי יוסי said 'a case like this is a גט.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the two used the same words about two different cases. רבי was talking about 'from today and after death,' and רבי יוסי about a גט written before the deadline and given after it. That is why their views should not be mixed together.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי and רבי יוסי both say 'a case like this is a גט,' but about different cases. רבי was talking about 'from today and after death.' רבי יוסי was talking about a גט written within twelve months and given after. So we cannot assume they agree.

phrases.english: What is the view of רבי יוסי? As we learned in a משנה:
"Write and give a גט to my wife,

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא בָּאתִי מִיכָּן וְעַד שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ״,
phrases.english: if I have not come back from now until twelve months,"
and they wrote it within the twelve months

phrases.aramaic: וּנְתָנוּהוּ לְאַחַר שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ – אֵינוֹ גֵּט;
phrases.english: and gave it after the twelve months — it is not a גט;
רבי יוסי says: a case like this is a גט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 14. It gives the source for רבי יוסי's phrase and closes this discussion.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי's 'a case like this is a גט' refers to a different case than רבי's.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about a גט written within twelve months and given after.

steps.title: New line of the משנה: a גט given 'if I die from this illness'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. A sick man gives a גט 'from today, if I die from this illness,' and then he gets up and walks in the market.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'This is your גט from today, if I die from this illness,' and he got up and walked in the market, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new topic. It quotes a line from the משנה to set up רב הונא's teaching in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband is sick and makes the גט depend on dying from this illness. The question is what happens when he gets better enough to walk around outside. This quote prepares for רב הונא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: If I die from this illness
He got up and walked in the market — he seemed to recover
Etc. — the rest of the line is in the משנה

phrases.aramaic: ״זֶה גִּיטִּיךְ מֵהַיּוֹם, אִם מַתִּי מֵחוֹלִי זֶה״,
phrases.english: "This is your גט from today, if I die from this illness,"
and he got up and walked in the market, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה גִּיטִּיךְ מֵהַיּוֹם, אִם מַתִּי מֵחוֹלִי זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of רבי and רבי יוסי and opens a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes the משנה's case of a sick man's conditional גט, and his getting up and walking in the market.

steps.title: רב הונא: a sick man's גט works like his gift
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא teaches that a sick man's גט is like his gift. If he gets up healthy, the gift is cancelled, and so is the גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: His גט is like his gift. If he gets up from his illness, his gift goes back to him. So too, if he gets up from his illness, his גט is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a rule that compares a sick man's גט to the gift of a שכיב מרע (a person on his deathbed).
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שכיב מרע's gift is given only because he thinks he is about to die. So if he recovers, the gift is cancelled. רב הונא says the גט works the same way: it was given only because of his expected death, so if he recovers, it is cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: His גט is like his gift
A gift — here, the gift of a שכיב מרע
He got up — he recovered from the illness
It goes back — it is cancelled

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule ties two areas of הלכה together. Like a deathbed gift, the גט only works if he dies the way he expected, so a recovery cancels it.

phrases.english: רב הונא said: His גט is like his gift;
phrases.notes: He means the gift a person gives while lying sick in bed, expecting to die.

phrases.english: just as his gift, if he got up — it goes back;
so too his גט, if he got up — it goes back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a rule for the משנה line quoted in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sick man's גט is like a שכיב מרע's gift. If he recovers, it is cancelled.

steps.title: A sick man's gift works without a formal act of acquiring, just like his גט
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא completes his comparison. A sick man's גט is given once he says 'Write,' even without saying 'Give.' In the same way, his gift works once he says 'Give,' even without a formal קנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And just as with his גט, even though he did not spell everything out, once he said 'Write' it is given even though he did not say 'Give,' so too with his gift: once he said 'Give,' it works even though no formal act of acquiring was done with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא is still talking. He shows a second way that a sick man's גט and gift follow the same pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A healthy man who says 'Write a גט' has not told anyone to give it. A healthy man's gift needs a formal קנין. For a שכיב מרע, his words alone are enough in both cases, because we follow what he clearly wants. This shows the גט and the gift are treated as one family of rules.

keyTerms.meaning: they made a formal act of acquiring with him (a קנין)

steps.whyThisMatters: This second parallel shows that רב הונא sees a sick man's גט and his gift as following the same rules. The challenge that comes next is aimed at his first parallel: that getting up healthy cancels the גט, just as it cancels the gift.

phrases.english: And just as his bill of divorce —
phrases.notes: 'His' means the sick man's, the same person רב הונא was talking about in the last step.

phrases.english: even though he did not spell it out,
once he said 'Write' —
[it is given] even though he did not say 'Give';
so too his gift:
once he said 'Give' —

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא קְנוֹ מִינֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: [it works] even though they did not make a formal acquisition with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה גִּיטּוֹ אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא פָּרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב הונא's statement from step 17 with a second parallel between a sick man's גט and his gift.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שכיב מרע's gift works when he says 'Give' with no קנין, just as his גט is given when he says 'Write' without saying 'Give'.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה: why assess how he died if getting up cancels the גט?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that if the man got up, walked in the market, then got sick and died, the court assesses which illness killed him. If getting up cancels the גט, as רב הונא says, the assessment would be pointless.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: 'This is your גט from today if I die from this illness,' and he got up and walked in the market, then got sick and died. The court assesses him: if he died from the first illness, it is a גט; if not, it is not a גט. But if you say 'once he gets up, it is cancelled,' why do I need an assessment? He already got up!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא using the משנה. According to רב הונא, the man's getting up should end the matter, with no need to check what he died from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said a sick man's גט is cancelled once he gets up healthy, just like his gift. The משנה, though, has the man getting up and walking in the market, and still asks which illness killed him. That implies the גט might still be valid even after he got up, which goes against רב הונא.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say his getting up cancels the גט. It says we check which illness killed him. That is exactly why it looks like a problem for רב הונא.

phrases.english: We learned in the Mishna:
'This is your bill of divorce from today,
if I die from this illness,'
and he got up and walked in the market,
and then got sick and died;
they assess him —
if he died because of the first illness,
it is a valid bill of divorce;
if not, it is not a bill of divorce.
And if you say 'if he got up, it is cancelled,'
why do I need an assessment?
He already got up!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: זֶה גִּיטִּיךְ מֵהַיּוֹם אִם מַתִּי מֵחוֹלִי זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's rule (steps 17–18) using the משנה quoted in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that a sick man's גט is cancelled if he gets up.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires an assessment of which illness caused death even after he got up and walked. That would make no sense if getting up automatically cancelled the גט.

steps.title: Answer: he passed straight from one illness into another
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרב יוסף, in the name of רבא, explains that the משנה is talking about a man who never truly recovered. He moved directly from one illness into another.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בריה דרב יוסף said in the name of רבא: the משנה means he passed from one illness into another illness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא by reading the משנה as a case where the man was never really healthy in between.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he never truly got better, רב הונא's rule (cancelled only once he gets up healthy) does not apply. The assessment is needed to figure out whether the first illness or the second one killed him.

keyTerms.meaning: he moved from one illness to another

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא:
phrases.english: Mar, son of Rav Yosef, said in the name of Rava:
[It is a case] where he passed from one illness to another illness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the משנה refers to someone who never fully recovered.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה describes a man who fully recovered, so the assessment would contradict רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: He went straight from one illness to another, so he never 'got up' in רב הונא's sense. The assessment decides which illness killed him.

steps.title: But the משנה says 'he got up'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the משנה's wording, 'he got up,' sounds like a real recovery.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה teaches 'he got up'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer by pointing to a word in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'He got up' seems to mean he got better, which does not fit a man who moved straight from one illness to the next.

keyTerms.meaning: but it teaches (pointing to wording in the source)

phrases.english: But it teaches 'he got up'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 20 from the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that he passed from one illness to another.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'עמד' suggests a real recovery.

steps.title: He got up from this illness but fell into another
steps.stepSummary: 'He got up' only means he was free of the first illness. He immediately fell into a different one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He got up from this illness and fell into another illness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the word 'got up' so that it fits the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Got up' refers only to leaving the first illness behind, not to becoming healthy. He was sick the whole time.

phrases.english: He got up from this illness,
and fell into another illness.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָמַד מֵחוֹלִי זֶה וְנָפַל לְחוֹלִי אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading a word in the source.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'עמד' means he left the first illness and went into a second one.

steps.title: But the משנה says 'he walked in the market'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects again: walking in the market sounds like a healthy person.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה teaches 'he walked in the market'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presses on a second phrase in the משנה that seems to show a full recovery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if 'got up' can be explained, going out to the market suggests he was well enough to live normally.

phrases.english: But it teaches 'he walked in the market'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to the answer of step 20, again from the wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that he was never truly healthy.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Walking in the market implies full health.

steps.title: He walked leaning on his cane
steps.stepSummary: He walked in the market only with the help of a cane, so he was still not healthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: He walked leaning on his staff.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains 'walked in the market' as weak walking with support, which keeps the answer in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking with a cane shows he was still sick. So רב הונא's rule, which applies only to a real recovery, is not contradicted by the משנה.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's assessment case is about a man who never truly recovered. That is how רב הונא's rule (a full recovery cancels a sick man's גט, just like his gift) still stands.

phrases.english: He walked on his staff;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23 and keeps the answer of step 20 intact.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading a phrase in the source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Walked in the market' means he was fully healthy.
steps.terutzMaskana: He walked only with a cane, so he was still ill.
